<!-- section:action -->

1. **Look at the crumb before changing anything.** Tight, even crumb with a pale crust points to fermentation; a flat, spread loaf points to structure.
2. **Check the starter record.** Was it at its peak when you mixed? See [read a starter by evidence](#/lesson/hearth-m01-l01).
3. **Recompute hydration including the starter**, as in [hydration and dough strength](#/module/hearth-m02).
4. **Change one thing** and bake again, writing down what you changed.

<!-- section:example -->

### Worked example: a fictional Tuesday loaf

The loaf was dense with a tight crumb. The starter had been mixed two hours after its peak, and the kitchen was cold. The baker kept the recipe, fed the starter later so it peaked at mixing time, and extended bulk fermentation by an hour. The next loaf opened up.

<!-- section:limits -->

This guide assumes a sourdough loaf baked at home. It does not diagnose flour quality problems, oven faults or enriched doughs, and a single bake is weak evidence: repeat a change before trusting it.
